name: Clinical Informatics Mgmt (MS)

rules.name: Course Requirements
rules.desc:
Students take a set of required courses during each of the four academic quarters. These courses reflect the overall set curriculum of the program and cannot be taken at alternative quarters. The required curriculum consists of six business courses, six information technology courses, an ethics course, and a practicum course. Currently, there are no elective courses offered through the program. The complete schedule of courses is listed. All courses are required. No substitutions are permitted.
To complete the Master's in Clinical Informatics Management, students must complete a minimum of 48 units. During quarters two, three, and four, students complete a practicum course, with the bulk of the effort for this course occurring in quarter four. MCiM courses must be taken for a letter grade.
rules.notes: CIM 202 will be taken over the course of four consecutive quarters, for a total of four units. CIM 200 will be taken over the course of three consecutive quarters, for a total of six units. CIM 215 must be taken over the course of two consecutive quarters, for a total of two units.

rules.name: MCiM Program Proposal
rules.desc: MCiM students are required to submit a program proposal at least two weeks before the final study list due date of their first quarter of enrollment. Due to MCiM’s set curriculum, a pre-filled proposal is available for MCiM students on the MCiM Resource Hub. Students must sign and submit the proposal to the MCiM administration; failure to do so is grounds for dismissal from the program. As there are no shifts in curriculum or electives allowed, there should be no need to revise the program proposal after submission.

grading: MCiM students must enroll in the required courses for a letter grade, and must enroll for the number of units detailed in the instructions.
policies:
Attendance Policy
MCiM is a one-year, full-time program designed to be completed across four quarters, with onsite class weekends held generally every other Friday and Saturday.
Attendance is central to the learning model. An "onsite session" refers to one day of an onsite class weekend. All missed sessions count toward a student's quarterly absence limit, including absences due to illness. Students are not able to join onsite classes remotely, and classes are not recorded for absent students.
Students must submit the MCiM Attendance Form at least one hour before the start of an on-campus class day to receive credit for advance notice. Advance notice should also be reported directly to instructors, except in emergencies. If the form is not submitted, the absence is treated as without advance notice.
Per quarter, the following limits apply:
With advance notice:

• 3 absences: warning

• 4 absences: academic probation and a required meeting with the MCiM Director of Graduate Studies

• 5 or more absences: dismissal from the program
Without advance notice:

• 2 absences: warning

• 3 absences: academic probation and a required meeting with the MCiM Director of Graduate Studies

• 4 or more absences: dismissal from the program
Students who anticipate difficulty maintaining good standing under this policy should contact the MCiM Admin Team before the start of the onsite weekend to discuss options.
transferPolicy:
The Master of Science in Clinical Informatics Management (MCiM) program does not allow students to transfer in credits. The MCiM program maintains a set curriculum for graduate students. MCiM students are required to enroll in the required courses set by the program.

Prior to each quarter's enrollment period, MCiM students will receive enrollment instructions with details of the courses required for minimum degree progress.
reviewNotes: Every course in the set curriculum is required, letter graded: the fourteen CIM courses, with CIM 200 over three quarters (6 units), CIM 202 over four quarters (4 units) and CIM 215 over two quarters (2 units), for 48 units. You check by hand the signed program proposal.
